articles.title: Successful Conclusion of the 20th Anniversary Annual Marine Technology Conference
articles.summary: The Hellenic Institute of Marine Technology (H.I.M.T.) successfully organised the 20th Annual Marine Technology Conference, held on 6 and 7 October 2026 at the Eugenides Foundation, preceded by a pre-conference event on 5 October at the V.Ships Auditorium in Piraeus. articles.body: The Hellenic Institute of Marine Technology (H.I.M.T.) successfully organised the 20th Annual Marine Technology Conference, held on 6 and 7 October 2026 at the Eugenides Foundation, preceded by a pre-conference event on 5 October at the V.Ships Auditorium in Piraeus. This year’s conference was of particular significance, marking the twentieth anniversary of an established institution that has become a reference point for scientific knowledge, technological innovation and collaboration across the maritime sector. With more than 900 registrations, the Conference brought together representatives from the shipping industry, academic & research institutions, public bodies and businesses, confirming the strong interest in the technological developments shaping the future of shipping. The Conference was officially opened by Mr. George Pratikakis, President of H.I.M.T., who highlighted the significance of the anniversary and the Conference’s longstanding contribution to scientific dialogue and the exchange of expertise. He emphasized that the Institute, founded in 1972, continues to operate as an independent scientific organization, bridging research, academic knowledge and the shipping industry. Emphasis was placed on the challenges of the energy transition, digitalization, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, with innovation and investment in human capital identified as essential prerequisites for the competitiveness of Greek shipping. articles.title: C.H. Robinson identifies five forces shaping freight markets in 2027
articles.summary: C.H. Robinson has released its 2027 Freight Market Outlook, identifying five major factors that could influence transportation costs, capacity and supply chain operations over the coming year. The report examines developments across ocean shipping, air freight, road transport, intermodal services and port operations....
articles.body: C.H. Robinson has released its 2027 Freight Market Outlook, identifying five major factors that could influence transportation costs, capacity and supply chain operations over the coming year. The report examines developments across ocean shipping, air freight, road transport, intermodal services and port operations. It highlights how regulatory changes, capacity pressures and geopolitical uncertainty could affect the movement of goods across global markets. According to C.H. Robinson, shippers will need to assess risks across different transport modes and prepare alternative arrangements to limit potential disruptions. Five factors influencing freight markets The outlook identifies transportation regulations as a key area to watch in 2027. Changes to safety requirements, emissions rules, customs procedures and cross-border compliance could affect operating costs and available transport capacity. Legal and liability developments are another concern. Rising insurance costs and changes in legal responsibilities could influence how logistics providers operate and price their services. The report also examines capacity growth. C.H. Robinson notes that an increase in overall transport capacity does not necessarily mean that sufficient equipment or services will be available on every trade route. Regional imbalances and demand for specialised equipment could continue to create constraints. Extreme weather is identified as a fourth factor, particularly because disruptions to ports, roads and other infrastructure can affect freight movements well beyond the areas directly impacted. articles.title: Taureana di Palmi Port redevelopment begins
articles.summary: The Conference of Services for the completion of the docks at the Port of Taureana di Palmi has concluded, enabling a EUR 7.5 million project that will significantly expand the port’s capacity, improve recreational boating services and integrate environmental and landscape enhancements into the Costa Viola coastal...
articles.body: The Conference of Services for the completion of the docks at the Port of Taureana di Palmi has concluded, enabling a EUR 7.5 million project that will significantly expand the port’s capacity, improve recreational boating services and integrate environmental and landscape enhancements into the Costa Viola coastal context. The project has been awarded to SILEM, Società Italiana Lavori Edili Marittimi, with construction scheduled to begin on November 3 and a duration of 20 months. The agreement was signed by the Port System Authority of the Southern Tyrrhenian and Ionian Seas, led by President Paolo Piacenza. The project will complete the shoreside docks, making the entire perimeter of the port’s waterfront fully docked, expanding the available port area and increasing the number of berths while improving navigation safety within the basin. Ground area works include paving of yards with porphyry slabs, construction of service infrastructure for safe port management, garages for nautical activities and facilities for boaters encompassing catering, nautical clubs, commercial services and restrooms. The project aims to transform the port from a mooring facility into a space connecting the port, the city and the sea, enhancing the tourist appeal of the surrounding area. Environmental sustainability has been given particular prominence. Excavated and dredged materials will be reused to nourish a stretch of coastline north of the port, maximising resource efficiency and limiting disposal requirements while strengthening the relationship between infrastructure development and coastal protection. New green areas will be created behind the caissons using native species consistent with the coastal environment, forming dune systems serving both environmental and landscape functions

articles.title: A.P. Moller Capital agrees to acquire Portek International
articles.summary: A.P. Moller Capital has signed an agreement to acquire 100% of Singapore-based port operator Portek International from Mitsui & Co. The transaction will be completed through the A.P. Moller Capital Emerging Markets Infrastructure Fund II. Founded in 1988, Portek operates a geographically diversified portfolio of...
articles.body: A.P. Moller Capital has signed an agreement to acquire 100% of Singapore-based port operator Portek International from Mitsui & Co. The transaction will be completed through the A.P. Moller Capital Emerging Markets Infrastructure Fund II. Founded in 1988, Portek operates a geographically diversified portfolio of multipurpose terminals serving domestic and international trade flows. The company has interests in seven terminals across Algeria, Gabon, Indonesia, Latvia, Malta and Vietnam. Portek also provides port engineering and operations and maintenance services, primarily from Singapore and Indonesia. The company employs approximately 1,400 people across its headquarters and operating businesses. Its terminals handle around seven million tonnes of bulk cargo, 700,000 containers and approximately 90,000 vehicles annually. Following completion, A.P. Moller Capital intends to work with Portek’s management and local operating teams to develop the business. Its priorities will include operational performance, governance, safety, capital discipline and environmental performance, including emissions-reduction planning. “Portek is a strong fit with our investment strategy and active owner philosophy,” said Semih Gökmen, Partner at A.P. Moller Capital. “It is an established business with a diversified portfolio of port operations serving important trade flows across three continents, supported by experienced local operating teams,” he added. Kim Thagaard Pedersen, Director at A.P. Moller Capital, said Portek represents a differentiated port platform with established positions across its markets. The acquisition expands A.P. Moller Capital’s transport and logistics infrastructure portfolio, which includes investments in Philippines-based AC Logistics and Bergé Logistics in Spain
takeaways: Moller Capital has signed an agreement to acquire 100% of Singapore-based port operator Portek International from Mitsui & Co.
The transaction will be completed through the A.P.

articles.title: Only 38% of UK operators use alternative fuel vehicles, GXO finds
articles.summary: Only 38% of UK transport operators surveyed are currently using alternative fuel vehicles, despite widespread efforts to reduce emissions, according to new research from GXO Logistics. The company’s latest Future of Transport report, published on 14 October 2026, surveyed more than 1,000 supply chain, transport and...
articles.body: Only 38% of UK transport operators surveyed are currently using alternative fuel vehicles, despite widespread efforts to reduce emissions, according to new research from GXO Logistics. The company’s latest Future of Transport report, published on 14 October 2026, surveyed more than 1,000 supply chain, transport and logistics decision-makers across the United Kingdom. The findings show that 87% of respondents consider emissions reduction a key priority. However, rising operating costs are increasingly influencing decisions about fleet investment. Some 63% said higher fuel costs are accelerating their interest in alternative fuel vehicles, while 76% believe that demonstrating cost savings or operational efficiencies is essential before committing to new investments. Operators focus on immediate cost savings High vehicle purchase costs, limited infrastructure and uncertainty over future fuel technologies continue to slow the transition. Instead, many businesses are focusing on improving the efficiency of their existing transport operations. According to the survey, 43% of respondents are reducing partially loaded journeys, while 41% are working to cut empty vehicle movements. Another 41% are exploring fleet sharing, and 39% are optimising delivery routes. All four measures have become more common since GXO’s previous survey in 2024. Investment in supporting infrastructure also remains limited. Only 25% of businesses have started planning investments in charging or refuelling facilities, while 30% have begun procurement planning for future energy requirements. Multiple fuel technologies expected to play a role The research suggests that UK logistics businesses do not expect a single technology to replace diesel across all transport operations. articles.title: Georgia Ports secures Army Corps permit for Savannah Container Terminal
articles.summary: Georgia Ports Authority has announced that the US Army Corps of Engineers has approved the permit for the Savannah Container Terminal following a three-year review process, with the announcement made by President Kevin Price at the annual State of the Port of Savannah event. Construction on the new terminal is...
articles.body: Georgia Ports Authority has announced that the US Army Corps of Engineers has approved the permit for the Savannah Container Terminal following a three-year review process, with the announcement made by President Kevin Price at the annual State of the Port of Savannah event. Construction on the new terminal is scheduled to begin in January 2028, with completion anticipated in the mid-2030s. The USD 2.3 billion Savannah Container Terminal will be located on Hutchison Island in Savannah, covering 350 acres and capable of handling the largest container ships. The facility will add 3.5 million TEUs of capacity, taking Savannah’s total capacity from its current 7.75 million TEUs toward the port’s long-term target of a 12 million TEU gateway container port. The terminal development is part of Georgia Ports’ US$ 5 billion infrastructure investment programme, described by GPA Chairman Alec Poitevint as the largest in the nation, building on the US$ 4.13 billion invested in port and inland infrastructure over the preceding decade. The Savannah Container Terminal announcement was accompanied by the disclosure that CEO Griff Lynch will retire on August 1, 2027, after 16 years with Georgia Ports. During his tenure spanning roles as Chief Operating Officer from 2011 and CEO, revenues have increased 213%, container volumes are up 90% and RoRo volumes have grown 60%. Lynch attributed the port’s trajectory to talented employees, a supportive board and the partnership of state government and agencies under Governor Kemp and the Georgia Legislature. The terminal permit follows other major ongoing investments, including the US$ 1.6 billion upgrade of Ocean Terminal from 200,000 TEUs to 1.75 million TEUs capacity, expected to be completed by the end of 2028.
takeaways: Construction on the new terminal is scheduled to begin in January 2028, with completion anticipated in the mid-2030s.

articles.title: Alabama port records strong revenue
articles.summary: The Alabama Port Authority has closed fiscal year 2026 with revenue of approximately US$ 245 million, an increase of more than 20% over the previous fiscal year, marking the strongest revenue year in the organisation’s history. The record result came just over one year after the Mobile Ship Channel reached its...
articles.body: The Alabama Port Authority has closed fiscal year 2026 with revenue of approximately US$ 245 million, an increase of more than 20% over the previous fiscal year, marking the strongest revenue year in the organisation’s history. The record result came just over one year after the Mobile Ship Channel reached its authorised depth of 50 feet on October 3, 2025, with increased customer demand, higher bulk cargo volumes, strong rail activity and the added capacity of the deeper channel all contributing to the outcome. Since the channel opened to its full depth, 168 vessels have transited with a recorded draft greater than 45 feet, enabling shippers to move more cargo per trip without the restrictions imposed by the previous channel depth. The US$ 425 million Mobile Harbor Modernization Project, a state-federal partnership between the Alabama Port Authority and the US Army Corps of Engineers, deepened and widened the ship channel for larger modern cargo vessels, with dredging beginning in 2020. In addition to the greater depth, the project widened a portion of the channel to enable two-way vessel traffic. The project was authorised by Congress in the 2018 Water Resources Development Act, with federal funding of more than US$ 270 million secured through the efforts of former US Senator Richard Shelby and Alabama’s congressional delegation. The State of Alabama invested US$ 150 million through the 2019 Rebuild Alabama Act to cover its share of the expansion and fund additional berth dredging, championed by Governor Kay Ivey with bipartisan legislative support. The channel expansion is part of more than US$ 2 billion in capital investments the Port Authority is making across the Port of Mobile, including a major container terminal expansion, development of inland rail facilities

Port Vessel and voyage Final departure Nansha Hazira Express 645S 22 November 2026 Singapore Hazira Express 649N 1 December 2026 Subic Bay Hazira Express 649N 10 December 2026 Following the withdrawal of the CPF service, Hapag-Lloyd will use third-party feeder services to handle cargo moving to and from the Philippines. The carrier will also restructure its Taichung Express service to retain coverage at Nansha. articles.body: Ellerman City Liners has appointed Gary Cobbing as its new Chief Executive Officer. Cobbing has worked within the GB Global Group for more than 17 years, holding several senior leadership positions across its shipping, logistics and supply chain operations. In his new role, he will lead Ellerman City Liners’ strategic direction, with responsibility for customer service, operational performance, network development and sustainable growth. His appointment comes as Ellerman City Liners continues integrating Viasea into its network. The integration is expected to expand the carrier’s shortsea capabilities, service portfolio and geographical reach across Europe. “I am honoured to be appointed Chief Executive Officer of Ellerman City Liners at such an exciting time for the business. We have strong foundations, a talented team and a clear vision for the future,” said Cobbing. “As global trade continues to evolve, our focus remains on delivering reliable, customer-focused shortsea shipping solutions while continuing to strengthen our network, enhance our capabilities and create value for our customers,” he added.
takeaways: Ellerman City Liners has appointed Gary Cobbing as its new Chief Executive Officer.
Cobbing has worked within the GB Global Group for more than 17 years, holding several senior leadership positions across its shipping, logistics and supply chain operations.
In his new role, he will lead Ellerman City Liners’ strategic direction, with responsibility for customer service, operational performance, network development and sustainable growth.
